title: Operator upgrade: interleaved config merge resolver and staged hotfix for on-prem tenant failures
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
After a staged operator + Helm release (customer-managed on-prem clusters), several tenants reported failed post-upgrade reconciliation and silent config divergence. Root cause analysis shows the operator path that merges Helm-generated values with tenant overrides had a race when two concurrent upgrade waves (staged canary -> regional -> remainder) interleaved value snapshots. The merge resolver was non-deterministic for array-typed and map-typed values containing placeholder tokens; in a small percentage of upgrade sequences the operator wrote a partially-merged config back into the tenant CR, which then became the source of truth for subsequent upgrades. That corrupted manifest state and led to CRD reconcile failures, webhook rejections (mutating webhook failed validation), and stuck helmRelease resources.

What happened (high level):
- Operator upgrade started with staged rollout across tenant groups.
- A background reconciler captured the tenant Helm values snapshot while a parallel reconciler applied a patch replacing placeholders.
- Interleaved writes produced a merged document with half-new, half-old structure (array vs scalar mismatches).
- Later upgrades and webhooks validated against the CRD schema failed, causing tenant pods to remain Terminating or Controller loops to OOM retry.

Impact:
- 12 tenants across 4 customers observed failed post-upgrade states (errors: webhook validation, invalid manifest field type, helmRelease stuck in pending).
- Customer escalations raised to SE and CS teams; two customers requested rollbacks and runbook support.

Reproduction steps (dev cluster):
1) Create two parallel upgrade workers simulating staged canary and regional batches.
2) Seed tenant CR with placeholder array field and tenant-specific override map.
3) Run upgrade with operator vX.Y.Z that includes the current merge resolver; trigger concurrent reconcile loops (sleep offsets).
4) Observe partially-merged CR written and subsequent validate/failures.

Short-term mitigations (already executed):
- Rolled targeted hotfix 1.20.1 to the operator image for affected tenants that disables the parallel-merge fast-path and forces single-writer reconciliation while we patch the merge algorithm. This was applied to customers that agreed to hotfix (PR + release notes linked in comments).
- Applied emergency webhook-sideguard to reject incoming mutated CRs that contain mixed-typed fields (prevents further state poisoning).
- Customer support performed manual CR sanitization for 8 tenants (scripted transforms, backups taken to S3 bucket s3://redwood-onprem-escalations/ENG-721314/).

Proposed long-term fix (implementation plan):
1) Replace current merge resolver with deterministic three-way merge using last-applied-annotation and explicit type-preservation rules (arrays replaced only when lengths match or when an explicit replace marker exists).
2) Add an operator-level optimistic-locking write path: write with server-side patch precondition on resourceVersion and retry if conflict, preventing interleaved partial-writes.
3) Add unit and e2e tests that simulate interleaved reconciles, including fuzzing of placeholder tokens and arrays.
4) Add telemetry that emits merge decisions and conflict counters to the Console dashboard (per-tenant histogram of merge retries and resolved-conflicts).
5) Create a migration job to scan on-prem tenants for mixed-typed fields and either auto-heal or flag for manual review depending on confidence score.

Acceptance criteria for release runtime-1.20.2: 
- No interleaved-merge failures in the staged experimental test harness after 2000 randomized runs.
- Migration job completes scan and auto-heals low-risk tenants without user action; high-risk tenants are listed in recovery playbook.
- Telemetry surfaces merge conflicts within 30s and ties to tenant-id for CS alerts.

Runbook snapshots and artifacts: 
- Recovery playbook created in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-721314+interleaved+merge+runbook
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/5123 (contains single-writer gate and webhook-sideguard)
- Sanitization script: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/eng/esc/ENG-721314/sanitize-scripts
- Customer notification templates used for the escalation channel: https://docs.redwood.ai/esc/ENG-721314-notice.md

Next steps this sprint:
- Finalize deterministic merge implementation (owner: Diego Morales).
- Add e2e test harness for concurrent reconciles (owner: Jun Park).
- Ship runtime-1.20.2 with migration job and telemetry (owner: Maya Chen).
